source: Copernicus Sentinel-1 (ESA), radiometrically terrain corrected (RTC) by Microsoft Planetary Computer
method: Change detection on VV gamma0 (5x5 speckle filter). Open-water flood: VV below -15 dB on the flood day and at least 3 dB darker than before. Flood among buildings and trees (double bounce): VV at least 3 dB brighter and ground within 6 m of the nearest permanent water. Permanent water: already below -15 dB before the storm.
terrain: Vexcel DTM (2025 aerial survey, ~2.4 m) fused with USGS 3DEP lidar: Vexcel where it agrees with the lidar within 1 m after removing its +0.75 m offset, lidar on water, under buildings and dense canopy

agreement.note: Drill extent = FEMA Harvey inundation outline (depth grid > 0), permanent water excluded. Precision = share of what the radar flagged that lies inside the drill extent. Hit rate = share of the drill extent the radar also flagged. Radar misses much flooding under dense canopy, so a low hit rate is expected here.

limits: Flooding under canopy and in dense streets often does not darken in radar; wind-roughened water can look bright. One snapshot (30 Aug 2017 12:22 UTC), not the peak everywhere.
